_comment: Checked-in CMake target graph. `links` is the sorted first-party closure;
`requires` records the preset that must build each entry.
The server row must remain headless. Cross-tier rows name deliberate
escapes; the graph check complements configure-time tier enforcement.
v0.9 adds delivery, bake, assetc and audio paths.
`delivery` sits above `assets` and `net`; `bake` stays separate from the
runtime and `assetc` owns filesystem access. `render` consumes `assets`, not
foreign-format parsers. The server remains headless.
v0.13 adds `network` - finding a peer, and being findable. It sits above
`net` and below every program, which is why four rows gained it at once and
no row gained anything else. It is `shared` and links only `core` and
`net`, so the server row is still headless and the cdn row still configures
on a machine with no Vulkan SDK.
v0.14 adds `resources` - the engine's built-in GLSL, moved out of `render`.
It is linked for its files rather than its symbols: `mono_add_program` stages
the shaders of every module a program links, so the rows that gained it are
exactly the rows that draw. The server row gained nothing and still stages no
shaders/ directory.
v0.15 adds `bakegraph` to `game` and therefore to every program that reads a
game file. A world carries its bake pipelines in its document, and the point
of the v0.13 split is that this edge is the document format and not the
importers - the server row gained `bakegraph` and still does not name `bake`,
which is the property `D00102` was about. That pair of facts is what this row
is here to keep true.
v0.15 adds `shadercheck`, and its row links nothing. It reads compiled SPIR-V
against the contract `SDL_CreateGPUShader` documents, so its input is a byte
stream a specification defines and it needs neither the engine nor a shader
compiler - which is why it is `shared` and unconditional where `contentimport`
is client-gated. No other row changed: nothing links it, and the tool's own
executable links `core` for `Arguments` the way `linecount` does.
v0.15 adds `msl` - SPIR-V to Metal Shading Language, and the only module here
that links nothing first-party at all. That is the row worth reading twice: it
is `client` because SPIRV-Cross is configured only for a client preset, and it
is a module rather than code inside `render` because there are two callers at
two times. `mono.tools/shadercross` translates the built-in shaders during the
build and `render` translates a `ShaderScript` while the engine runs, and one
implementation is what stops those two from putting a texture on different
Metal indices. The rows that gained it are exactly the rows that already had
`render`; the server row gained nothing and still links no shader tooling.
v0.16 adds `loadtest` - many real replication clients in one process, for
measuring a server under load. Its row is the one worth reading for what it
does *not* name: no `render`, no `input`, no `audio`, no `ui` and no
`client`. A virtual client here is a socket, a connector and a store, which
is the whole reason two hundred of them fit in one process where two hundred
`client --headless` processes would be a measurement of the GPU driver. No
other row changed: nothing links it.

v0.17 adds `discord` - what a person's Discord profile says while an Atomic program is running. It is `shared` and links only `core`, which is why all five program rows gained it at once and no row gained anything else. The server row is still headless and the cdn row still configures on a machine with no Vulkan SDK: the module is a unix socket and a JSON writer, and it deliberately does not link `net` - Discord is a desktop application on the same box rather than a peer on a wire.

v0.19 splits `script`. It was 33,157 lines across 88 source files and half of that was binding glue for two VMs held apart by a filename convention, checked by a sixty-line CMake closure walk in the module's own CMakeLists. There are four rows now: `script` at L9 with **no vendor at all** - the port, the object model glue and the services, all VM-free; `scriptluau` and `scriptjs` at L10, one adapter each and neither able to name the other; and `scripthost` at L11, which is the one switch on `Language` plus every suite that has to see both VMs to check that they agree. The closure walk is deleted: the tier and layer checks say the same thing for free. `game` and `examples` moved from L10 to L12 because both call `MakeRuntime` and the factory is now above the adapters; nothing but the program band links either, so the move cost two `layer` fields and no edge.

v0.19 adds `sourcecheck`, and its row links nothing for `shadercheck`'s reason: it reads first-party C++ as text, so it needs neither the engine nor a configured build, and it is `shared` and unconditional. It checks the four rules `docs/CODE_ARCH.md` §11 listed as convention until this version - a private copy of data the ECS owns, a pointer inside a type marked as crossing a world boundary, a `core::Name` serialised as its `Id()`, and a header under `include/` that nothing outside its module includes. No other row changed: nothing links it, and the tool's own executable links `core` for `Arguments` the way `linecount` does.

v0.19 gives `msl` its one first-party edge: `core`, for the log. It was the only module here linking nothing of ours, and the index assignment it exists to perform is invisible - a texture on the wrong `[[texture(n)]]` samples somebody else's map on macOS and draws correctly on Linux. Both callers already link `core` (`mono.tools/shadercross` names it directly), so no program closure changed and no other row moved. What the empty row was protecting was that nothing in `msl` has an opinion about shaders, and that still holds.

v0.19 moves `nodegraph` out of `mono.engine` and into `mono.studio/nodegraph`, and its row loses its `layer` rather than gaining one. It is `client` tier, links nothing first-party, carries Dear ImGui and four concurrency headers, and exactly one target in the repository links it: `studio`. That is an editor widget library, and root `AGENTS.md` says `mono.engine` ships nothing on its own. Dropping the `layer` puts it in the program band, which is the half that is checked: `CheckTargetGraph.cmake` refuses an edge from anything that has a layer to anything that has not, so no engine module can start linking it without the check naming the edge. No other row changed - the closure was already `studio` alone.
